summary:
BlindRev is a Windows investigation game that turns NISAR radar data into a playable case file. You're an investigator watching NISAR passes over California's San Joaquin Valley, where groundwater pumping sinks the land around the California Aqueduct. Scrub through time, flip between optical imagery and real NISAR L-band backscatter, pick two acquisition dates, and draw the region you think is still subsiding. Your polygon is scored against a hand-drawn answer mask using IoU, precision, and recall.

We built it for the NASA Space Apps SAR challenge to teach the reasoning InSAR analysts use. A strange signal on one pass might be just atmosphere; real subsidence keeps showing up pass after pass. Telling those apart is the heart of the game. When the satellite didn't acquire data, the gap stays a gap — nothing is interpolated to fill it.
The location, pass dates, GIBS context imagery, and propagated orbit are all real. Displacement values are the one simulated piece: deterministic, and labelled SIMULATED everywhere they appear, so nobody mistakes the game for a monitoring product.

Subsidence is a slow, easy-to-miss threat to water infrastructure, and radar is the right tool for watching it — clouds and darkness don't get in the way. InSAR has always lived inside expert software, out of reach for everyone else. BlindRev hands that same evidence to players and lets them do the reasoning themselves.
details: BlindRev is a Windows desktop investigative game that combines satellite change detection with a guided evidence seeking. As an investigator in the BlindRev bureau, the user reads a mission briefing, scans through discrete satellite acquisitions, draws a Region of Interest around a suspected environmental anomaly, and validates that ROI against an authored reference change mask. The visual identity is Outpost Signal, which means "Follow the changes." Find the evidence.
